# Verification analysis: split-dns-authority-centos-stream10

Job: `2026-09-06__00-21-44`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> Each router answers DNS for the private network it serves. Have `node1`
> resolve the name `app.internal` to `node3`'s address for hosts on `lan-a`,
> and `node2` resolve the same name to `node4`'s address for hosts on `lan-b`,
> so each host reaches the service on its own side of the transit network by
> that one name.

## Environment

- Systems: **1 vyos + 1 opnsense + 2 centos-stream10**
- Networks: **mgmt, transit, lan-a, lan-b**
- Control node: **node3**
- Executor model: **claude-sonnet-5**

## Trial `split-dns-authority-centos-strea__CakvJ3H`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** Both split-horizon DNS requirements are directly satisfied with verification via both direct queries to each router and each host's own default system resolver: node1 (pdns-recursor) resolves app.internal to 10.10.10.10 for lan-a, and node2 (Unbound) resolves it to 10.20.20.10 for lan-b. These resolutions were re-verified after a full, sequential restart of all four nodes, and the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots corroborate that each node genuinely rebooted and recovered. Hygiene is good: the only notable mutations beyond the final configuration were a bounded, fully-reverted topology-discovery phase (temporary addressing plus tcpdump) and two opaque base64-encoded config-editing scripts on node2 whose effects were independently confirmed.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.850 | 0.900 | 101/18 (+10 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** node1 (VyOS) resolves app.internal to node3's address (10.10.10.10) for hosts on lan-a
  - **Why:** node1 was configured with pdns-recursor authoritative-domain 'internal' containing an A record app->10.10.10.10, listening on 10.10.10.1 restricted to the lan-a subnet (cmd-ae93ceb789344ba1, cmd-d2ac80eca47f4b4b). A dig query issued from node3 (10.10.10.10) against the router at 10.10.10.1 returned 10.10.10.10 (cmd-f30d99e6472f4c5e), and node3's own system resolver (via getent hosts, using /etc/resolv.conf pointed at 10.10.10.1) also returned 10.10.10.10 (cmd-5105ed11a74a4a64). This resolution persisted after a full restart of node1 (cmd-fd9776b77afb44bc, cmd-e1a7cf784e9840c4).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ae93ceb789344ba1`, `cmd-d2ac80eca47f4b4b`, `cmd-f30d99e6472f4c5e`, `cmd-5105ed11a74a4a64`, `cmd-fd9776b77afb44bc`, `cmd-e1a7cf784e9840c4`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** node2 (OPNsense) resolves app.internal to node4's address (10.20.20.10) for hosts on lan-b
  - **Why:** An Unbound host override app.internal -> 10.20.20.10 was added to node2's config and confirmed present in the rendered /var/unbound/host_entries.conf after an unbound restart (cmd-30388a2f6de8424b, cmd-ec27a376a7a54369). ### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.850**. Topology discovery used temporary /30 addresses and tcpdump captures on node1/node2/node3/node4 interfaces to identify physical links, since no topology documentation existed; all temporary addresses were flushed and tcpdump processes killed once discovery finished (cmd-0e53673f41384a85, cmd-4b483ed279084b9b), and temp files/logs were removed at the end (cmd-c8047f109f3e4d61, cmd-e8ef8983cd824e26). This was a bounded, low-risk, and reverted exploration necessary to establish a prerequisite (correct interface-to-network mapping) given missing documentation, not an unnecessary mutation. Two OPNsense config.xml edits were applied via base64-encoded inline Python scripts (cmd-9542b3cdb3a44ed8, cmd-30388a2f6de8424b) whose exact contents are not visible in the transcript, reducing transparency of that mutation even though its effect (the app.internal host override) was independently verified afterward. bind-utils and iputils packages were installed on node3/node4 (cmd-24406cfe3d454146, cmd-642c25310cb34561, cmd-f30d99e6472f4c5e) to support diagnostics/verification and were left installed; this is a minor, low-risk residual footprint rather than a harmful mutation. One long-running diagnostic command timed out server-side (cmd-31dd5a1fd1574b70) and its orphaned process was subsequently killed (cmd-103735ae422b46bb), which is corrective cleanup rather than a new problem. No failed or conflicting services, no weakened security controls, and no damaged package state were observed in the final snapshots.

### Comments and limitations

- The exact contents of two base64-encoded Python scripts used to edit OPNsense's config.xml (cmd-9542b3cdb3a44ed8, cmd-30388a2f6de8424b) are not visible in the transcript, so the precise mutation logic could not be independently reviewed, only its resulting effect.
- node3 and node4 reboot acknowledgements were observed indirectly via connection-reset/timeout errors immediately following the reboot command rather than a clean acknowledgement string, though the subsequent boot-identity change and recovery confirm the reboot occurred.
- DNS cache-size was set to 0 on node1's forwarding config as part of the authoritative-domain setup; this is a minor implementation detail not required or forbidden by the task and does not affect the material outcome.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.850); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
